the stratigraphy of slope channels is a record of the processes of bypass, erosion, and deposition.
slope channel fills in the Tres Pasos formation are dominated by bypass and erosion, with sedimentation occurring in the upper reaches of the channel system.

the nature of slope channels, their fill, and the processes that govern the evolution of these enigmatic features.

the record of slope channel fills is a record of sediment bypass, erosion, and deposition.
slope channels, as they evolve and are filled with sediment, record the processes and events of sediment bypass, erosion and deposition, and the relative magnitude of each of these processes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sediment-routing system is a complex and dynamic system that is sensitive to the relative magnitude of sediment supply versus sediment bypass, which in turn, is sensitive to a number of variables, including the rate of sediment supply, the rate of sediment transport, and the rate of channel incision.
the record of sediment transfer and bypass is more common than the record of sediment deposition within slope channels.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the record of slope channel fills is not a simple record of the processes that are active at any given time, but instead a composite of the sedimentary processes that have operated during the full life cycle of the channel.
outcrop is the best place to examine the full channel cycle and the processes of erosion and bypass that are critical for understanding the evolution of sediment-routing systems in the deep sea.
the sedimentary record in outcrop can provide a wealth of information about the sedimentary processes that are difficult or impossible to directly measure in the deep-sea.
